item.title: Dein Weg zu Bitcoin – Bitcoin lernen: Wo finde ich gute Inhalte? Bianca über die Gründung von BitUcation - Dein Weg zu Bitcoin
item.description:
Wer anfängt, sich mit Bitcoin zu beschäftigen, steht schnell vor einem Berg: tausende Videos, Podcasts, Bücher, Kurse – und dazwischen jede Menge Lambo-Versprechen. Genau vor diesem Problem standen auch Bianca und Caddy. Allerdings von der anderen Seite: Auf dem Weg in den Urlaub planten sie einen Workshop und fragten sich, wie der eigentlich zu den Menschen kommt, die sich dafür interessieren.Aus dieser Frage wurde BitUcation: eine Plattform, die Bitcoin-Bildung aus der ganzen Community an einem Ort bündelt.Wo findet man eigentlich gute Bitcoin-Inhalte, wenn man nicht weiß, wem man trauen kann?In dieser Folge erzählt Bianca, Mitgründerin von BitUcation, wie aus einer Urlaubsidee eine Plattform wurde, warum Dezentralität ihr Herzstück ist und wohin die Reise gehen soll. Und sie teilt sehr offen ihren eigenen Weg zu Bitcoin, der nicht über Rendite führte, sondern über ein IT-Netzwerk und einen Schicksalsschlag.👉 Warum man sich von der Informationsflut nicht erschlagen lassen sollte und bei den eigenen Fragen bleibt👉 Warum es nicht die eine richtige Quelle gibt, sondern die, bei der man sich gut aufgehoben fühlt👉 Warum Bitcoin-Bildung so schwer ankommt, solange es als Spekulationsobjekt gilt👉 Wie die BitUcation-Karte dir einen Ansprechpartner direkt in deiner Nähe zeigt👉 Warum Missionieren nicht funktioniert und ein echtes Bedürfnis alles verändertIch bin selbst BitUcator. Trotzdem habe ich in diesem Gespräch noch einmal verstanden, was hinter der Plattform steckt: kein Projekt, das Menschen überzeugen will, sondern eines, das da ist, wenn jemand bereit ist.✅ Die Gründungsgeschichte: von der Workshop-Planung zur Plattform✅ Selbstlernkurse, Live-Workshops, Webinare und zusätzliche Ressourcen✅ Warum Bitcoin-Bildung gerade aus einer privilegierten Lage heraus schwer ist✅ Die Vision: alle Menschen im DACH-Raum erreichen, auch im Mainstream💬 Zitat der Folge:„Bitcoin ist für mich ein Werkzeug, das mich hoffnungsvoll in die Zukunft blicken lässt.“📲 Bianca bzw. BitUcation findet ihr hier:• https://bitucation.com ✨ Mein Ziel: Bitcoin verständlich und greifbar machen durch Geschichten, die jeder nachvollziehen kann und die zeigen, dass die ersten Schritte nicht groß sein müssen und dass jeder Zweifel am Anfang hatte. Gefällt dir die Folge?Dann lass ein 👍 da, abonniere den Kanal und schick die Episode an jemanden, der das hören sollte 🚀📌 Schreib deine Fragen/Meinungen in die Kommentare – ich lese alle!⚡ Unterstütze den Podcast über Fountain: Auf Fountain kannst du die Audio-Version hören und mir freiwillig Sats per Lightning senden – ganz ohne Werbung oder Abo. 👉 https://fountain.fm/show/WdHajypwLY2JOQN2zH1S📲 Folge mir auch gerne auf Instagram: 🔗 https://www.instagram.com/finanz.bewusstsein Rechtlicher Hinweis: Dieser Podcast dient der finanziellen Bildung und persönlichen Meinungsäußerung und ist keine Finanz- oder Anlageberatung. Bitcoin ist volatil, Investitionen können zu Verlusten führen. Jede Entscheidung triffst du eigenverantwortlich. Study Bitcoin.Partner:🧡Bitcoin21 – stylische Bitcoin Kleidung:Mit dem Code FINANZB bekommst du 10 % Rabatt auf deine gesamte Bestellung. https://bitcoin21.shop/?ref=FINANZB 🧡Coinfinity – Bitcoin Börse :https://coinfinity.co/bitcoin-appCode: FINANZB - Damit sparst du 21 % deiner Gebühren in den ersten 6 Monaten.🧡21statues – Bitcoin Lampen und Statuen:https://21statues.de?sca_ref=10285598.SH2VZ7SHVa8Code: FINANZB - Du sparst 5 % auf alle ProdukteWeitere Empfehlungen und Codes:🧡BitBox – Cold Wallet:https://shop.bitbox.swiss/?ref=tfjnborqCode: FINANZB - Du sparst 5 % auf alle Produkte🧡Seedor – Backup-Lösung in Stahl:https://www.seedor.io/discount/FINANZB Code: FINANZB - Du sparst 5 % auf alle Produkte#bitcoin #podcast #finanzen #finanzbildung #bitcoineducation #bitcoinbildung #geld #bitcoinpodcast #deinwegzubitcoin

item.title: The Bitcoin Matrix – Aaron Siri: The One Product You Can't Sue in America
item.description:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

🎙️ GUEST

Aaron Siri — Managing partner of Siri & Glimstad. Lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN). Author of the new book Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines.

item.title: Der Relai Bitcoin Podcast – Zwei Freunde, eine Mission: Bitcoin verständlich machen, Manuel & Jonas von Bitcoin verstehen | Relai Bitcoin Podcast #131
item.description:
Manuel & Jonas sind die Hosts vom beliebten Podcast, Bitcoin verstehen. Darin bringen sie mit spannenden Videos, Tutorials, sowie Interviews dem Zuschauer die Grundlagen und Ideen hinter Bitcoin näher.

Im Gespräch mit Relai-CEO Julian Liniger sprechen die beiden über ihre Erfrahrung als Podcast Hosts, weshalb sie sich dazu entschieden haben den Podcast zu lancieren, wie sie Anfängern Bitcoin näherbringen, und was als Nächstes ansteht.

Folge Bitcoin verstehen auf X: https://x.com/BTCVerstehenPod

Oder abonniere den Podcast hier: https://bitcoinverstehen.info/

—

⏱ Kapitel:

item.description:

item.title: Swan Signal Live - A Bitcoin Show – John Haar Returns: Why the Fed Must Talk Tough While It Inflates
item.description:
• John reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as a nothing burger for Bitcoiners: a Fed chair must talk tough on inflation because signaling anything else would send inflation expectations and yields higher, while the long-run path of financial repression stays the same
  • Warsh reported that 54% of PCE basket components rose more than 3% over the past year, called 4.1% unemployment full employment, and framed inflation as squarely the Fed's problem to solve
  • Markets read the speech as hawkish anyway: the two-year yield rose about 12 basis points while gold and Bitcoin each gave back roughly 3.5%
  • On last week's expanded Treasury buybacks, John points to two signals: a 30-year yield near 5.3% is clearly bothering policymakers, and the Fed has never meaningfully reduced its holdings of 10-year-plus Treasuries even during quantitative tightening, evidence that natural buyers of long-dated government paper are scarce
  • The hosts revisit the shallowest bear market thesis they developed together on this show: a roughly 52% drawdown against 77% to 90%-plus in prior cycles, with the June low of $58,000 sitting just below the 200-week moving average before price rocketed back through it
  • John explains why he believes the June low will hold, while framing the 50-week moving average near $82,000 as the level the market is watching to declare a new bull market
  • Glassnode data shows 1.05 million Bitcoin of long-term holder supply with a cost basis between $83,000 and $86,000, the first heavy resistance shelf above spot, and the hosts discuss how cost basis shapes market psychology
  • The debasement trade is back in ETF volumes, with GLD and IBIT both in the top ten most traded funds, and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio breaking its year-long downtrend after gold's 2025 outperformance
  • Bitcoin's long correlation with software stocks broke down in June, and John argues it was always the wrong frame, a point Lyn Alden's Wall Street Journal essay makes at length: Bitcoin is a protocol of value, not another technology stock
  • A broad Treasury ETF has returned roughly negative 18% after inflation over fifteen years while the supply of government debt keeps expanding, the picture John says is quietly ending the era of Treasuries as the world's default store of value

item.title: Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock'n'Roll – Public Blockchains: The Roadblocks to Institutional Adoption
item.description:
What happens when a bank needs to freeze a token, but other network participants can see that instruction before it takes effect? And how should an institution respond when anyone can send unwanted assets to its blockchain address?

In this episode of Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock’n’Roll, Wee Kee Toh of Kinexys by J.P. Morgan and Michael Maurer of MIT’s Digital Currency Initiative examine the practical challenges of bringing regulated finance onto public blockchains. Drawing on their joint research, they explain why infrastructure built for open participation can create costly operational and compliance problems for financial institutions.

The discussion focuses on four challenges: transaction front-running, transaction omission or censorship, unsolicited tokens, and the risk of gas fees reaching sanctioned entities. These issues extend beyond familiar debates about trading profits or network performance. A pending freeze can be front-run, an urgent instruction can be delayed, and returning an unwanted token may require reviewing an unfamiliar smart contract.

What can institutions do? Toh and Maurer explore private transaction pools, encrypted mempools, heartbeat-based pause mechanisms and proposals to strengthen transaction inclusion. They explain which risks banks can mitigate themselves and where changes to protocols, governance or regulatory guidance may be needed.

The conversation also examines the trade-offs behind permissioned public networks and layer-two infrastructure. More control may help institutions manage risk, but it can alter the openness and decentralization that attract users in the first place.

For smaller banks, the decisive question may be whether participation is affordable. If every institution must build its own expensive safeguards, shared infrastructure could remain accessible mainly to the largest players.

A discussion about the requirements, responsibilities, and compromises that will shape institutional adoption of open blockchain networks.

What would make public blockchains practical for regulated financial institutions—not just technically accessible?

Topics covered:
- Front-running and MEV: why transaction ordering matters for asset freezes, emergency pauses and other institutional controls.
- Censorship and transaction inclusion: the potential role of private transaction submission, encrypted mempools and fork-choice inclusion lists (FOCIL).
- Unsolicited tokens: why token spam can create monitoring, smart-contract review and compliance burdens for banks.
- Sanctions exposure: the difficulty of controlling who receives gas fees and the limits of application-layer address checks.
- Infrastructure trade-offs: public permissioned networks, layer twos and the balance between institutional control and decentralization.
- Regulatory clarity: proposed guidance on unsolicited tokens, reasonable sanctions controls and safe-harbour provisions for unavoidable residual exposure.

The discussion distinguishes potential safeguards from complete solutions. A central question is how to make compliance manageable for a broader range of institutions, rather than only those able to commit substantial resources.

Research and guests:
- Public Blockchains and Regulated Financial Institutions
- Wee Kee Toh on LinkedIn
- Michael Maurer on LinkedIn

item.title: Rob Wallace | Bitcoin News – The $107T Hole American Can't Ignore Anymore | Joe Consorti & Parker Lewis
item.description:
⚪ Ready to run Bitcoin yourself? Shop miners, hardware wallets, nodes and home servers at Solo Satoshi: https://www.solosatoshi.com/?utm_campaign=bitcoinnews&utm_source=bitcoinnews&utm_medium=bitcoinnews

There are roughly $6-7 trillion actual dollars in the system and $107 trillion in dollar-denominated debt — and no amount of growth fixes that math.

Rob sits down with Joe Consorti and Parker Lewis to break down why inflation and high rates are hitting at the same time, why Hank Paulson's "break the glass" warning should worry everyone, and why AI's coming deflationary wave will collide head-on with a financial system that depends on constant money printing. They also dig into what the Ledger supply chain attack means for self-custody, and go head-to-head on whether Bitcoin treasury companies are helping or confusing Bitcoin's path to adoption.

Here is what we cover:

• Why red-hot inflation and high rates are happening at the same time, and why that breaks the Fed's playbook

• The $107 trillion debt math problem that can't be grown out of

• Why AI's deflationary force collides with a financial system built on constant money printing

• What the Ledger attack means for self-custody, multisig, and eliminating single points of failure

• The debate over whether Bitcoin treasury companies and "digital credit" products help or distort Bitcoin's price

Subscribe so you never miss an episode breaking down what's really happening with the economy and Bitcoin.

TIMESTAMPS

0:00 Intro: The $107 Trillion Debt Problem

1:06 Inflation Comes In Red Hot

39:01 Why Decentralization Still Matters

41:55 Coldcard vs. Ledger: Comparing the Attacks

item.title: Onramp Bitcoin Media – Your VPN Knows Too Much | Carl Dong
item.description:
A traditional VPN sends your entire internet history through one company that also has your name, address and payment details. Liam sits down with Carl Dong, founder of Obscura VPN and former Bitcoin Core developer, on why two hops beat one and why AI makes privacy urgent.


Guest: Carl Dong, founder of Obscura VPN and former Bitcoin Core developer:

X: https://x.com/obscuravpn

Website: https://obscura.com/


BOOK A CONSULTATION

Holding Bitcoin for decades raises two questions: who protects it, and how it reaches your family. Onramp answers both. Three institutions protect it, and no single one can lose it, move it, or use it. Inheritance built in. Insured through Lloyd's of London. Speak with our team to see if it fits.

👉 https://go.onrampbitcoin.com/consult-fs-pod


GET ON THE LIST

• Onramp: our research, event invites, and the week's Bitcoin news in one free email. https://go.onrampbitcoin.com/research-fs-pod

• Early Riders Insights: the best content in the ecosystem, weekly. https://www.earlyriders.com/research


ABOUT THIS EPISODE

Carl Dong grew up building ways around China's Great Firewall, then worked at Blockstream and Chaincode Labs on Bitcoin Core, where his focus was software supply chain security. He explains reproducible builds and fuzzing, and why AI's infinite patience turns theoretical attacks into real ones. He makes the case that a traditional VPN swaps your ISP for one unregulated company that sees all of your traffic, and walks through Obscura's two-party relay with Mullvad, where neither company knows both who you are and where you go. He covers disguising VPN traffic as HTTP/3 to get through firewalls in airports, hotels and China, and why privacy tools have to be as easy as the alternatives. Liam and Carl also discuss AI agents overtaking human web traffic, connected AI that may know you better than anyone, private and local models, and how recent hardware wallet supply chain attacks harden the industry.


CHAPTERS

00:00 - Carl Dong: from the Great Firewall to Bitcoin Core

03:15 - The VPN trust problem and the two-party relay idea

06:29 - AI, infinite patience and software supply chain attacks

08:41 - Reproducible builds: verifying Bitcoin Core downloads

11:15 - How a traditional VPN works and what it can see

14:25 - VPNs as custodians: don't trust, verify

19:18 - Freedom tech has to be easy to use

ABOUT THE SHOW

item.title: bitcoin ist - Wissen statt FOMO – 24) ... Energie mit zwei Leben
item.description:
Bitcoin und Energieverbrauch werden oft in einem negativen Zusammenhang genannt. Diese Folge zeigt ein differenzierteres Bild: warum Bitcoin-Mining Stromnetze stabilisieren kann, wie aus Abwärme ein zweiter Wertschöpfungskreislauf entsteht, und wo die Grenzen dieser Entwicklung aktuell noch liegen.

Themen in dieser Folge:

  • Wie sich der Anteil nachhaltiger Energien beim Bitcoin-Mining seit 2022 entwickelt hat
  • Warum der Ausbau von Wind- und Solarenergie ein Netzstabilitätsproblem mit sich bringt
  • Wie Bitcoin-Miner als flexible Last genutzt werden können, um Lastspitzen abzupuffern
  • Warum jede Kilowattstunde beim Mining "zwei Leben" bekommt: Bitcoin-Belohnung und nutzbare Wärme
  • Drei Unternehmen, die das bereits umsetzen: Terahash, 21energy und Power2Bit


Die Anfangs erwähnte Studie der Cambridge University

https://www.jbs.cam.ac.uk/2025/cambridge-study-sustainable-energy-rising-in-bitcoin-mining/


Erwähnte Unternehmen:

  • Terahash – Bitcoin-Mining Infrastruktur für Unternehmen
  • 21energy – Bitcoin-Heizungen für Privathaushalte und Kleingewerbe
  • Power2Bit – flexible, klimaneutrale Rechenzentren und kommunale Wärmeplanung


Hinweis: Die genannten Prozentzahlen zum Energiemix variieren je nach Berechnungsmethode (konservativer Netzmix vs. direkte Unternehmensmeldungen) und waren zum Zeitpunkt der Aufnahme aktuell.

]]>

item.title: The Bitcoin Layer – Bitcoin Wants To Run But Liquidity Won’t Let It
item.description: <![CDATA[In this episode, Demian explains TBL’s analysis of why bitcoin is holding up even as liquidity hit its lowest point of the cycle. He covers how the TBL Liquidity Index works, what a red dot actually signals, and why bitcoin’s own supply and demand have shifted in its favor as the sellers ran out and more than 70% of supply moved into profit. He closes on the three things that would need to ease for liquidity to turn.]]>

item.title: Unchained – Ledger Wallets Were Drained of $100 Million. Is Self-Custody Still Safe?
item.description:
A hidden implant read Ledger seed phrases off the screen and sent them out over an eSIM. Mark Karpelès and SEAL 911's Jonty discuss what that means for self-custody.

========================================================

Thank you to our sponsor!

  • Put your crypto to work with Nexo: earn daily interest or borrow funds against your assets on one platform trusted by more than 10 million clients.

    Find out more at ⁠https://unchainedcrypto.com/go/nexo-podcast-sn⁠.

    Geo-restrictions, eligibility and terms apply.

========================================================

Quick favor: We're deciding what Unchained does next; new shows, stream times, what's worth paying for.⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ Our listener survey⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ takes five minutes, it's anonymous, and I read the write-in answers myself. Everyone who takes it can enter a drawing for a free year of Unchained Premium or Bits + Bips Premium. Open through Sunday, October 18.

— Laura

========================================================

An estimated $100 million or more has been drained from Ledger hardware wallets sold through CryptoBilis, an authorized reseller in Southeast Asia. The devices carried a hidden implant that reads the seed phrase off the screen and sends it out over an eSIM.

Jonty, founder of Pangolin Intelligence and a SEAL 911 contributor, and Mark Karpelès, CEO of Karpelès Lab, join Laura Shin to trace how the attack was found and how far it may reach.

They cover drains dating back to September 8, a tampered Ledger Flex bought from Metapod at Singapore's airport, the two MediaMarkt devices a buyer in Europe traced to distributor Aqipa, and Tether's $10 million freeze.

Mark argues Ledger's manual sends mixed signals by picturing the device's insides while warning that opening it voids the warranty, then opens a Nano X on camera to show what to look for.

The open question is whether self-custody's best defense against malware has become its newest attack surface.


Host:

  • ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Laura Shin⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠, Host / Unchained

Guests:

  • ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Mark Karpelès - CEO of Karpelès Lab Inc.

  • ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Jonty - Founder of Pangolin Intelligence and Contributor to SEAL 911

Timestamps

🎬 00:00 Intro

🚨 03:50 How Jonty spotted the Ledger drains through SEAL 911 victim reports

📡 05:52 How the implant reads a 24-word seed phrase and sends it out by eSIM

🛫 11:33 Mark on the spy implant he found in a Ledger Flex bought in Singapore

🕵️ 15:16 CryptoBilis or a distributor? Mark and Jonty on who could be behind it

📣 17:38 Nexo: Generate daily interest on your crypto or borrow against your assets at https://unchainedcrypto.com/go/nexo-podcast-yt

🇪🇺 18:19 MediaMarkt and Aqipa: has the Ledger implant reached Europe?

🛒 27:00 Buying direct vs. through a reseller, and why Vietnam needs resellers

🔐 31:30 Ledger's 'tamper-proof' notice and whether self-custody is dead

🔧 36:45 Mark opens a Nano X on camera to show how to check for an implant

🧊 40:33 Tether's $10M freeze and why Jonty says recovery could take years

item.title: Bitcoiners - Live From Bitcoin Beach – What Happens to Your Bitcoin If You Die? How a Texan in El Zonte Built a Free Tool for Your Family | Eric Summers of The Bitcoin Hardware Store
item.description:
What happens to your Bitcoin if you die tomorrow? In El Zonte, one builder’s answer is a dead man switch and an encrypted seed phrase.

If you practice self custody, your 12 or 24 words are stored somewhere safe. How your family would ever reach them is the question Eric Summers set out to solve.

Mike first met Eric as the math tutor for one of his son’s friends.

Eric’s story of moving to El Salvador begins in Texas in 2023, when a Salvadoran friend told him to come look. He stayed 10 days with his friend’s parents in San Salvador and flew home sure the country checked all his boxes. Then he loaded everything he owned into a Toyota Tacoma and drove to El Salvador, a month down the Pacific coast through Mexico and Guatemala. Border agents took his drone headset for night vision goggles. What they took his telescope for, you’ll have to hear from him.

He found El Zonte, started working at the Bitcoin hardware store, and saw what was missing. He’d venture to say 90 to 95% of Bitcoiners have no recovery method for their families.

So he built two free, open source tools. One encrypts your seed phrase so thoroughly that he says you could post it on Twitter. The other is the dead man switch, an email check-in that sends your beneficiary the final key if you stop clicking for three months, six months, or a year.

Then Mike asked about the weak point. If your heir loses their key, the Bitcoin is gone. Eric’s answer is in the episode.

Living in El Salvador gave Eric a second job too. For expats living in El Salvador on the coast, the bilingual college prep schools are in the capital, so he tutors homeschool families one on one.

This is why El Salvador is such a good place to build!

Whether you hold your own keys with no plan for your family, or you’re weighing a move to El Zonte, listen to this one.


—Bitcoin Beach Team


Learn more about Eric Summers:
X: https://x.com/ericscalibur
X (store): x.com/tbhs_sv

https://www.stayatbitcoinbeach.com/punta-mango-villas

Live From Bitcoin Beach

item.title: Stephan Livera Podcast – Debanking and Bitcoin Business Accounts in the EU | Prashanth Chandrashekar SLP782
item.description:
Prashanth Chandrashekar argues that much of Europe's debanking comes down to how banks score transfers. Money arriving from a crypto exchange's account is treated as a higher-risk third-party payment, while a transfer between two accounts in your own name passes with far fewer flags. Bringin's answer is a named virtual IBAN for each customer, which he says lowers the risk of being debanked rather than removing it.

Prashanth, who is from India, started Bringin after moving to Estonia holding Bitcoin and finding he couldn't easily spend it. He now runs the company's consumer app and its new business accounts.

They cover MiCA's licensing reset, which by his figures left only about 30% of earlier firms licensed but lets the survivors passport across the EU; accounts closed without explanation under tipping-off rules; and how named IBANs differ from the deposit IBANs exchanges hand out. On the consumer wallet, built on Spark, he is direct about the trade-offs: operators are mostly centralized and can see payments, though they cannot move funds alone.

On Bringin for Business, he describes pilot users such as mining-rig sellers paying suppliers abroad, plus stablecoin support and accounting exports. The custody model differs from the consumer app: keys sit in a hosted Turnkey enclave with spending policies, Bringin holds an extra key in multi-director setups, seed export is discouraged, and ownership changes run through Bringin's backend. Third-party euro payments were promised within days of recording, and corporate cards are not yet available.

Disclosure: Stephan is a small investor in and advisor to Bringin.

item.title: The Café Bitcoin Podcast – The Finale: Liquid's 4,000 Bitcoin, the Caching Bug, and 50 Days for Freedom Wrapped
item.description:
• The last day. Brady opened with the count, 37 shows in 50 days, and the campaign's frame: political independence 250 years ago, monetary independence now. Yan Pritzker, Frank Corva, Suze and Alec on stage; Unseen Finance returned at the end.
  • The Liquid hack, plainly. On Sunday somebody sent 4,000 L-BTC to SideSwap's peg-out and the Liquid Federation paid out real Bitcoin. The L-BTC had been created from nothing. Blockstream paused the sidechain and 3,400 Bitcoin came back Monday.
  • ⭐ Yan on what broke: a caching bug, not anyone's keys. "The only two hard problems in computer science are naming and cache invalidation." Two transactions shared one cache key, so validators mistook a fake for one already checked.
  • Why it is not Bitcoin. Yan: Liquid is an 11-of-15 federation of companies with its own database and rules. "This is a separate thing, this is not Bitcoin itself." Lightning is built on Bitcoin script; Liquid is not.
  • ⭐ Frank on the 15%. The hackers returned 85% and kept about 600 Bitcoin. His question: will anyone be made whole, and if they keep it, "they're surely not white hats." A Bitcoin Policy Institute lawyer offered to talk.
  • Yan's verdict on the hat color: gray. Taking everything to beat a black hat is arguable. Keeping a cut is not. "You don't just return a wallet and take a bunch of stuff out of it."
  • Suze's question: Bitcoiners are ruthless about added trust assumptions, so why did Liquid get a pass? "Were we discerning enough?" Leave the base layer and you take on another code base and another set of failure points.
  • ⭐ Yan on open source in the AI era: it stays because every open project gets red-teamed by the whole internet. Closed systems get hacked too, "we just don't hear about them." The base chain is "the ultimate boss" nobody has beaten.
  • Yan's bank numbers, read live from the Identity Theft Resource Center: 3,332 reported data compromises in 2025 affecting 280 million people, 739 of them in financial services. "Bank-grade security" is not a standard anyone actually meets.
  • ⭐ Frank's hard question: must the layers be as bulletproof as Bitcoin? Yan: nothing is, and the only path is slow growth. Bitcoin was attacked at $1, then $10,000, then a billion. Early adopters carry the risk.
  • Yan's rocket-ship rule. Bitcoin Core engineering is closer to launching a spacecraft than shipping web software. "Years of careful review, study, simulations on other chains." Test new tech on other coins for two years first.
  • Suze asked whether ossification risks losing the skills to change Bitcoin in 50 years. Frank and Yan: no. Ossification is no new features, not no developers, and AI has widened who can work on cryptography and game theory.
  • Yan on open-weight versus hosted AI: the same debate as open source versus closed, and open source won the internet. His advice to companies: externalize memory, skills and harness so you can swap models. Swan built its own.
  • Unseen Finance returned with a proposal: these incidents are a credibility problem for the services on top of Bitcoin, not for Bitcoin. His fix, borrowed from banking: a self-regulatory body plus an insurance pool that service providers pay into.
  • Brady's tally at the close: Cory, Yan, Steve, Alec, Isaiah, Matt and Brandon from Swan; Larry Lepard three times; Parker Lewis, Daniel Batten, Tom and Callum, Guy Swann, Ryan MacLeod, Alana, Bob Burnett, Roxana. Suze made 35 of 37.
  • The close. "We have the tools, we have the knowledge, we have the culture, we have the determination." The half-price buy fee ends today; limit orders placed today keep it. Yan's last word: take security seriously, "go play with AI."
    • ]]>

item.title: No Second Best - A Bitcoin Podcast – Did the Federal Reserve Just Open the Door to Bitcoin?
item.description:
Jamie Dimon just went on national television to push back against Bitcoin and crypto legislation. Hours later, a Bitcoin exchange gained direct access to the Federal Reserve's settlement rails.

At the same time, Morgan Stanley filed for a spot Bitcoin ETF while geopolitical tensions escalated in the Middle East and Bitcoin surged.

This episode breaks down the growing conflict between the traditional banking system and the emerging Bitcoin financial infrastructure, and why the global monetary system may already be bending toward neutral, hard money.

]]>

item.title: The Bitcoin Frontier – Inside Wall Street’s bitcoin playbook with Denny Galindo
item.description:
Denny is a wealth manager and bitcoin research lead at Morgan Stanley, where he bridges traditional finance and bitcoin for high-net-worth investors. He operates inside one of the world’s largest financial institutions while developing frameworks to help advisors understand and allocate to bitcoin.

In this episode, Denny joins The Bitcoin Frontier to share how investors should think about bitcoin in a portfolio, the three core investor buckets driving adoption, and his thoughts on determining whether you’re underweight or overweight bitcoin. We dig into bitcoin’s market cycles and seasonal framework, the role of global money supply in driving returns, and practical strategies for gaining exposure in a volatile asset.

TIMESTAMPS:
0:00 – Intro & Denny’s role bridging traditional finance and bitcoin
2:00 – From equity research to leading bitcoin insights at Morgan Stanley
4:20 – The three investor buckets: digital gold, venture, and diversifier
7:30 – How institutions evaluate volatility and correlation
10:50 – Where bitcoin fits in portfolios today (risk asset vs store of value)
14:00 – How to determine if you’re underweight or overweight bitcoin
18:00 – Why most investors are still early (0–4% allocation range)
21:40 – Will the three investor frameworks converge over time?
23:10 – Bitcoin cycles: macro liquidity vs halving-driven supply shocks
26:30 – Using cycles for rebalancing vs long-term holding strategies
31:20 – Tail risks: quantum computing and “earthquake” scenarios
36:10 – Bitcoin as a global store of value and M2-driven returns
41:10 – Modeling long-term returns: monetary expansion + adoption
48:30 – How to build a position: dollar-cost averaging and timing
52:15 – Seasons of bitcoin: winter, spring, and portfolio adjustments
55:00 – What it takes for bitcoin to become a standard portfolio allocation

item.title: Thank God for Bitcoin – TGFB Episode 83: A Candid Conversation with Rapper and Truth-Teller, Zuby
item.description:
Zuby (@ZubyMusic) joins Jordan Bush for a wide-ranging conversation about faith, courage, and what it takes to be a positive voice in a divided world. He tells the story of his path from independent rapper to one of today's most recognizable social commentators, and how the COVID era pushed him to start speaking out. He also reflects on the upbringing that shaped his character.

From there, Zuby and Jordan dig into the ideologies shaping public discourse: gender norms, privilege, victim mentality, and the grievance culture that keeps people divided. Zuby makes the case for empowerment over resentment, for solutions over complaints, and for a sturdier definition of love and care. He closes by sharing how his faith has grown, why he worries about the UK's loss of national pride and purpose, and why he still believes optimism and individual responsibility can change things.

Rapper. Author. Speaker. Coach. Host @ZubyPodcast

'Strong Advice' book https://zubymusic.gumroad.com/l/zubyfitness

]]>

item.title: Crypto Nerds Podcast - Krypto, Bitcoin, Web3 & Co. – Uncut | Krypto News: Ledger-Implantat, Haltefrist vertagt und Chipbeben in Korea
item.description:
Eine Woche, in der es an jeder Ecke brannte. Seit dem 9. Oktober melden Ledger-Kunden in Südostasien leere Wallets. Ursache ist ein Hardware-Implantat, das die Recovery Phrase beim Einrichten vom Display abgreift und per Mobilfunk an die Angreifer schickt. Der Schaden liegt laut On-Chain-Analysen bei rund 93 Millionen Dollar aus über 300 Wallets, betroffen sind Geräte des Resellers CryptoBilis (Malaysia, Indonesien, Philippinen). Am 11. und 12. Oktober zeigt ein Nutzer dann Implantate in Geräten von europäischen Händlern, darunter eines aus einem deutschen MediaMarkt. MediaMarktSaturn hat den Verkauf vorerst gestoppt, Ledger prüft. Eric ordnet ein, was das für die Frage "Hardware Wallet oder regulierte Börse" bedeutet.

In Berlin kam die Wende einen Tag vor dem Kabinettstermin: Der Referentenentwurf zur Krypto-Steuer hängt in der Ressortabstimmung, am 14.10. wurde nicht beschlossen. Zuvor hatten Nicole Nowak und Dr. Ingo Heuel im Petitionsausschuss erklärt, wen die Abschaffung der Haltefrist wirklich trifft: nicht die Trader, sondern die, die langfristig vorsorgen. Über 44.000 Unterschriften haben die Anhörung möglich gemacht.

Dazu: Die US-Inflation steigt im September auf 3,7 Prozent statt der erwarteten 3,6, Bitcoin rutscht am Donnerstag kurz unter 80.000 Dollar. Der chinesische Speicherhersteller CXMT kündigt eine neue DRAM-Architektur mit 30 bis 50 Prozent mehr Dichte an, Samsung und SK Hynix verlieren an einem Tag 7 und 10 Prozent, der Kospi fällt um 5,5 Prozent. Und die ESMA gibt Kryptobörsen in der EU bis zum 8. Januar 2027 Zeit, nicht MiCA-konforme Stablecoins wie USDT aus dem Angebot zu nehmen. Warnhinweise reichen ausdrücklich nicht.

In dieser Folge erfährst du

wie das Ledger-Implantat funktioniert und welche Geräte betroffen sind warum der Fall nicht auf Südostasien beschränkt bleibt und was MediaMarkt getan hat wie Eric die Frage Hardware Wallet oder MiCA-Börse für sich beantwortet was im Petitionsausschuss gesagt wurde und wen die Haltefrist-Abschaffung trifft warum das Kabinett am 14.10. nicht entschieden hat und was das für den 1.1.2027 heißt was 3,7 Prozent US-Inflation für die Fed und den Bitcoin-Kurs bedeuten warum eine Ankündigung aus China den Kospi einbrechen lässt und was das über Klumpenrisiken im S&P 500 sagt was bis zum 8. item.title: THE Bitcoin Podcast – Bitcoin Taxes, Inheritance & Knowing When You Have Enough | Jessy Gilger
item.description:
How much Bitcoin is enough—and what is it actually for? Jessy Gilger, CFP® and founder of Verify Wealth, joins Walker to connect Bitcoin conviction with the practical work of taxes, inheritance, cash flow, and making time for the people you love.

We discuss why your legal documents, financial plan, and Bitcoin keys need to agree; how unclear inheritance instructions can burden a grieving family; and how tax planning fits into a life built around Bitcoin. Jessy also explains the idea behind Bitcoin Scholars Fund and why “stay humble, stack Saturdays” matters just as much as stacking sats.

item.title: House of Satoshi - Bitcoin und Friends – #67 Zana Iseni: Bankerin am Tag, Bitcoinerin in der Nacht
item.description:
Zana Iseni wollte ihrem Partner Bitcoin ausreden und hat sich dabei selbst überzeugt. 2016 schickte sie ihm noch einen Artikel über «gefährliche Kryptowährungen», heute ist Bitcoin ihre grösste Leidenschaft.


Tagsüber arbeitet Zana in Risk Control und regulatorischem Reporting einer Bank. Abends ist sie Mrs. Zatoshi: Bitcoin-Educatorin auf Instagram und LinkedIn, Keynote-Speakerin und Mitgründerin von Satoshis Daughters.


Mit Rino spricht sie über teures Lerngeld, über Bitcoin für Einsteiger und darüber, warum sie beim Wallet-Setup sogar die Brille abzieht.

  • Bitcoin speichert Lebenszeit: Lohn ist das Ladegerät, Fiat ein Akku, der in der Schublade leerläuft
  • Warum sie als Bankerin lange nicht über Bitcoin reden wollte
  • Buy the dip oder Sparplan? Was der Fear & Greed Index taugt
  • Seed Phrase selber würfeln, mit Bleistift aufschreiben, Setup nie verraten
  • Don’t trust, verify: die Sache mit dem Kokoswasser

item.title: Bitcoin.com News Interviews – Matt Hougan: Bitcoin Bottomed in June. Is the Next Bull Market Here?
item.description:
Has Bitcoin already bottomed, and are we entering the next bull market?


Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan joins Alex Richardson and David Sencil to explain why he believes Bitcoin bottomed in June and has since entered an early-stage bull market, despite potential volatility surrounding the U.S. midterm elections.


Hougan breaks down why Federal Reserve rate cuts may matter less than many investors think, how inflation, recession and government intervention could shape Bitcoin’s next move, and why institutional adoption still has significant room to grow.


The conversation also explores the future of Bitcoin self-custody, Bitwise’s investment thesis on NEAR and AI agents, the growth of tokenized assets, and why central-bank Bitcoin adoption could become one of the market’s most important yet overlooked narratives.

item.title: BITCOIN & ALTCOINS – Hohe Zinsen, starker Dollar: Was Bitcoin und Altcoins jetzt bewegt
item.description:
Bitcoin und viele Altcoins haben wieder nachgegeben. Sie notieren erneut in Kursbereichen, die sie zuvor endlich verlassen hatten. Könnte genau das die Basis für den nächsten Anlauf sein?

Derzeit bremsen hohe Anleiherenditen, steigende Ölpreise und ein stärkerer US-Dollar den Kryptomarkt. Sollte dieser Gegenwind nachlassen: Welche Signale sprechen für eine Trendwende, und worauf kommt es in dieser Woche an?

Darüber sprechen Oliver Michel von der tokentus investment AG und Johanna Krämer in der neuen Folge von "BITCOIN & ALTCOINS".

Hinweis: Die im Podcast besprochenen Coins und Token stellen keine spezifischen Kauf- oder Anlageempfehlungen dar. Die Moderatoren oder der Verlag haften nicht für etwaige Verluste, die aufgrund der Umsetzung der im Podcast diskutierten Gedanken oder Ideen entstehen.

Das Gespräch wurde am 13.10.2026 an der Frankfurter Börse aufgezeichnet.

item.title: The Bitcoin Infinity Show – You Don’t Own Your Bitcoin | Stephan Kinsella | BIS #225
item.description:
Stephan Kinsella joins the Bitcoin Infinity Show to talk about why you can’t legally own Bitcoin, what the difference between ownership and possession means for self-custody, and whether the July 2026 Coldcard hack was really theft. Knut and Stephan dig into Austrian economics, libertarian contract theory, why fractional reserve banking is harder on a Bitcoin standard, and how Bitcoin could limit the state’s ability to borrow and tax. They also look back at the Property and Freedom Society’s 20th anniversary in Bodrum, Murray Rothbard’s centennial, Hans-Hermann Hoppe’s split with the Mises Institute, and their Austrian economics panel at BTC HEL in Helsinki.

item.title: VERIFIED by Bitcoin Suisse – He Co-Wrote the Paper Behind Modern AI. Then Built NEAR
item.description:
His grandparents' life savings ended up in a Soviet bank book that became worthless. As a kid in Ukraine, he watched bread prices rise exponentially. Years later he co-authored the paper behind modern AI, and he's convinced AI and crypto belong together. 

Illia Polosukhin, co-author of "Attention Is All You Need" and co-founder of NEAR, joins Bitcoin Suisse to explain how the transformer actually works, why he left Google to start NEAR as an AI company in 2017, and why he thinks we've done almost nothing to prepare our systems for a post-AGI world.

]]>

item.title: Krypto Corner – Bitcoin, ETF und NFT: Sicher investieren - Krypto verstehen und sicher starten – Episode #19: Brücken mit Geländer – Cross-Chain | Krypto Corner
item.description:
Episode 19: Brücken mit Geländer – Cross-Chain


Ein Klick von Ethereum nach Arbitrum – und plötzlich steht der Ladebalken still. In der Berliner WG testen Max, Sophie, Julian und Tom eine Cross-Chain-Brücke mit zehn USDC. Was ist jetzt wichtig: warten, prüfen oder noch einmal senden?


In dieser ausführlichen Folge der Krypto Corner begleiten wir die Überfahrt und erklären, welche Sicherungen hinter einer Bridge stecken. Die Handlung basiert auf Kapitel 19 meines Buchs; die Atmosphäre und Dialoge wurden für den Podcast erweitert.


In dieser Folge erfährst du:

• Wofür Cross-Chain Bridges gebraucht werden und warum sie attraktive Angriffsziele sind.

• Wie Lock-and-Mint als eines von mehreren Brückenmodellen funktioniert und warum die Deckung zählt.

• Wie du offizielle Adressen, Netzwerk und Token prüfst – und was ein kleiner Testbetrag bestätigen kann, ohne spätere Sicherheit zu garantieren.

• Warum ein hängender Ladebalken keinen Grund für eine panische zweite Sendung bietet und angeblicher Support niemals deine Seed Phrase erhalten darf.

• Welche eigenen Verwahrungs-, Gegenpartei- und Gebührenrisiken ein Umweg über eine zentrale Börse mitbringt.

• Warum du die Gebühren für spätere Transaktionen auf der Zielkette vorher klären solltest.

• Weshalb ein „Transfer“-Label in der Steuersoftware keine rechtliche Einordnung ersetzt und Eigenübertrag, Tokenwechsel und Wrapping unterschieden werden müssen.


Die Gebührenbeispiele aus dem Buch sind keine aktuellen Preiszusagen. Steuerliche Fragen in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz benötigen eine Prüfung des konkreten Vorgangs und deiner persönlichen Situation.


📖 Das Buch zur Show:

„Krypto verstehen – sicher starten. Band 1“ von Sascha Swen Heiter

https://amzn.eu/d/06DuLLUw


🎧 Spotify:

https://open.spotify.com/show/5MOMwCZpWNvm6J52jkdLcl

Apple Podcasts:

https://podcasts.apple.com/de/podcast/krypto-corner-bitcoin-etf-und-nft-sicher-investieren/id1872914214

Instagram:

https://instagram.com/Swen_Heiter


⚖️ Rechtlicher Hinweis:

Podcast und Beschreibung dienen ausschließlich der allgemeinen Information und Unterhaltung. Keine Anlageberatung, Finanzberatung, Rechtsberatung oder individuelle Steuerberatung. Kryptowährungen, DeFi, Smart Contracts und Cross-Chain Bridges bergen erhebliche Risiken bis zum Totalverlust. Audits und erfolgreiche Testtransfers garantieren keine Sicherheit. Zentrale Anbieter haben eigene Verwahrungs- und Gegenparteirisiken. Es gibt keine garantierten Renditen. Steuerliche Regeln können sich ändern und hängen von Land, Vorgang und persönlicher Situation ab. Software-Ergebnisse ersetzen keine fachliche Prüfung. Ziehe für individuelle Entscheidungen qualifizierte Beratung hinzu.


Werbung für mein eigenes Buch und meinen Podcast. KI-unterstützte dramaturgische Erweiterung der Original-Buchszene; technische und steuerliche Erläuterungen wurden aktualisiert. Die Erzählerstimme ist meine autorisierte ElevenLabs-Corner-Stimme.


]]>

item.title: 21Focus - Der Bitcoin-Unternehmer Podcast – Aus der Banken IT in die Welt von Bitcoin - Harald Betz
item.description:
Folge #61 – Ein Gespräch über Banken IT und Bitcoin Bücher

Harald Beetz ist seit fast 20 Jahren selbstständig in der Beratung für Banken und Rechenzentren. Angefangen als Banklehrling bei der Sparkasse, hat er früh den Wandel von Beratung hin zu reinem Vertrieb erlebt und sich auf IT-Projekte spezialisiert. item.title: POD256 | Bitcoin Mining, Freedom Tech, and Awesome Tangents – 129. No Adult Supervision: AI Harnesses, Mining Stats, and Digital Security Theater
item.description:
In this episode, we flew without adult supervision and covered a wide range of territory, starting with reviving old hardware and ending with the future of Bitcoin, mining, and digital sovereignty. We talked about breathing new life into a 5K Intel iMac with Linux, the growing excitement around AI-native Linux environments, and eco’s early journey into self-hosting AI on a Mac Mini. A big part of the conversation focused on the difference between models, harnesses, and agents, and how these tools are quickly becoming essential for development work, including open-source Bitcoin and mining projects. We also dug into the tradeoffs between self-hosted AI and frontier subscription models, plus the security implications of increasingly powerful AI-assisted tooling.

From there, we shifted into the darker side of the digital world: broken identity systems, security theater, data breaches, and the growing fragility of centralized financial and authentication infrastructure. That naturally led us back to why Bitcoin matters, both as a tool for sovereignty and as something that still needs better usability and stronger open-source infrastructure. We wrapped with network stats, a look at mining pool centralization, some exciting updates around the 256 Foundation, a shoutout to our donation pool hashers, and a preview of the Proto rig headed our way. We also highlighted the importance of open-source mining firmware, the momentum behind Mujina, and why opening up the mining stack remains one of the most important jobs in Bitcoin.

]]>

item.title: The Peter McCormack Show – #222 - David Wood - We are The Last Generation Of Normal Humans
item.description:
Dave Wood is a pioneer of the smartphone industry, former senior executive at PPsion and Symbian and Chair of London Futurists. Having predicted the smartphone revolution in the 1990s, he now maps out the next radical phase of human evolution - from the reversal of biological aging to artificial superabundance.


Moving away from sensationalised doomsday narratives, Dave breaks down why humanity is approaching the end of "normal" unaugmented existence and how technological breakthroughs in the coming decades will make biological death optional.


We discuss:

•⁠ ⁠Why this is likely the last decade of "normal" unaugmented human beings.

•⁠ ⁠⁠How early smartphone pioneers accurately predicted large touchscreens but missed social media addiction.

•⁠ ⁠⁠The concept of "Longevity Escape Velocity" and why biological death can be abolished.

•⁠ ⁠⁠Why people are psychologically terrified of contemplating the end of aging.

•⁠ ⁠⁠How humans will spend decades inside vibrant, simulated digital worlds. The reality of AI agents breaking out across the internet and the need for chip-level guardrails.

•⁠ ⁠⁠How "Sustainable Superabundance" could make energy, health, and basic necessities too cheap to meter.


- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

item.itunes:summary:
Dave Wood is a pioneer of the smartphone industry, former senior executive at PPsion and Symbian and Chair of London Futurists. Having predicted the smartphone revolution in the 1990s, he now maps out the next radical phase of human evolution - from the reversal of biological aging to artificial superabundance.


Moving away from sensationalised doomsday narratives, Dave breaks down why humanity is approaching the end of "normal" unaugmented existence and how technological breakthroughs in the coming decades will make biological death optional.


We discuss:

•⁠ ⁠Why this is likely the last decade of "normal" unaugmented human beings.

•⁠ ⁠⁠How early smartphone pioneers accurately predicted large touchscreens but missed social media addiction.

•⁠ ⁠⁠The concept of "Longevity Escape Velocity" and why biological death can be abolished.

•⁠ ⁠⁠Why people are psychologically terrified of contemplating the end of aging.

•⁠ ⁠⁠How humans will spend decades inside vibrant, simulated digital worlds. The reality of AI agents breaking out across the internet and the need for chip-level guardrails.

•⁠ ⁠⁠How "Sustainable Superabundance" could make energy, health, and basic necessities too cheap to meter.

item.title: Bitcoin Country Podcast – Parker Lewis, Max & Stacy: Gradually, Then Suddenly
item.description:
Got something to say to this podcast? Send a voicemail, and you might hear yourself on the next episode!

Parker Lewis is the author of "Gradually, Then Suddenly" and Head of Business Development at Zaprite, working on Bitcoin payments after four years building collaborative custody at Unchained.

This conversation on X Spaces yesterday with Parker, Max Keiser, Stacy Herbert, and moderator Jethro Toro covered...

  • Parker’s path from Wall Street to Bitcoin: Deutsche Bank during the 2008 financial crisis, then Hayman Capital, where studying how the Fed would unwind quantitative easing led him down the Bitcoin rabbit hole in 2016
  • The story behind Gradually, Then Suddenly: an introduction to Saifedean Ammous, an early manuscript of The Bitcoin Standard, and reasoning through the most common questions about Bitcoin
  • Why self-custody is still so important: the Silicon Valley Bank failure, the fragility of the banking system, and multisig collaborative custody
  • Bitcoin as a Medium of Exchange: why payments are what let Bitcoin stand apart from the fiat rails, and Parker’s work at Zaprite
  • Texas and El Salvador: “Bitcoin Country” and the “center of hash” and why freedom-minded people move to Bitcoin-friendly jurisdictions
  • Bitcoin Histórico: a unique OG Bitcoin conference experience, where people can learn from the best speakers who have been in Bitcoin since the early days, at El Salvador’s National Palace, including Parker’s talk “Bitcoin Is Not a Panacea”

Join us for the full Freedom Month experience this November:

📍 10th · Bitcoin Capital Summit

📍 11 & 12 · BitcoinHistorico.com

(use code “COWBOY21” for 21% off)

item.title: Epicenter - Learn about Crypto, Blockchain, Ethereum, Bitcoin and Distributed Technologies – The DAO Security Fund: Turning a Historic Hack into Ethereum's Future | Griff Green
item.description:
Ten years after The DAO hack changed Ethereum forever, Griff Green returns to Epicenter to discuss the next chapter: the DAO Security Fund.


As a co-initiator of The DAO, Griff shares the untold story of recovering funds after the hack, why over 75,000 ETH remained untouched for years, and how its staking yield is now funding public goods for Ethereum security. The conversation also explores a provocative idea: Ethereum is incredibly secure—but still not safe for everyday users.


Topics covered:

1. The inside story of The DAO and its recovery

2. Why the DAO hack may be the only hack where everyone made money

3. The DAO Security Fund and funding Ethereum security

4. Quadratic funding, grants & public goods

5. Why phishing and UX remain Ethereum's biggest weakness

6. Can Ethereum become safer than traditional banks?

7. The future of safer wallets, OpSec, and the Ethereum Economic Zone


If you enjoyed the episode, don't forget to subscribe for more conversations with the builders, founders and investors shaping the future of crypto.

item.title: 21talk – Bitcoin-Steuer-Schock: Trifft es bald auch Gold? | 21weekly mit Marek Szabelski
item.description:
In dieser Ausgabe von 21weekly diskutieren Dino Heinert und Marek Szabelski die aktuellen Entwicklungen rund um die Bitcoin Steuer und das drohende Ende der einjährigen Bitcoin Haltefrist in Deutschland. Nach der Anhörung im Finanzausschuss und Petitionsausschuss des Deutschen Bundestages steht die steuerfreie Veräußerung nach § 23 EStG im Fokus. Neben den politischen Debatten über einen möglichen Bestandsschutz und den vertagten Kabinettsbeschluss analysieren die Experten, welche Parallelen zur Gold Besteuerung und dem physischen Edelmetallhandel bestehen. Dabei liefern sie fundierte Einblicke zu Krypto-Regulierungen, der Initiative pro-haltefrist.de und den wirtschaftlichen Konsequenzen für Privatanleger und Krypto-Investoren in Deutschland.Im zweiten Teil beleuchten Dino Heinert und Marek Szabelski den Sicherheitsvorfall um manipulierte Ledger Hardware Wallets und den daraus resultierenden Verkaufsstopp im Einzelhandel bei MediaMarkt und Saturn. Im Detail wird der Supply-Chain-Angriff erklärt und aufgezeigt, welche Risiken für die Eigenverwahrung und die Sicherheit privater Keys (Seed Phrase) entstehen. Krypto-Anleger erhalten wertvolle Praxis-Tipps zu Multisig-Lösungen, Phishing-Schutz, Hardware-Wallet-Sicherheitsprüfungen und der optimalen Verwahrung von Bitcoin und Assets abseits von zentralen Krypto-Börsen.Marek Szabelski:https://mareksz.substack.comHaltefrist erhalten:https://prohaltefrist.de/


(00:00) Intro (00:26) Zukunft der Bitcoin-Haltefrist & Petitionsausschuss (01:46) Kabinettsbeschluss vertagt & Bestandsschutz (02:34) Einschätzung der Anhörung durch Marek (04:28) Wird jetzt auch Gold besteuert? (05:22) Gold- vs. Bitcoin-Besitz in Deutschland (Studie) (08:08) Allianz mit der Gold-Lobby? (09:56) Infos & Initiative pro-haltefrist.de (11:01) Manipulierte Ledger-Wallets & Lieferketten-Angriff (12:33) Verkaufsstopp bei MediaMarkt & Saturn (13:11) Wo lag die Schwachstelle? (15:21) Vertrauenskrise bei Hardware-Wallets & Eigenverwahrung (18:26) Wichtige Sicherheits-Tipps für Hardware-Wallets (20:42) Multisig vs. Diversifikation über mehrere Wallets (21:56) Phishing, Betrug & Wachsamkeit (24:18) Fazit

]]>

item.title: Bitcoin für Frauen – Folge 7 – Bullen, Bären und Bitcoin-Zyklen: Warum der Kurs steigt und fällt
item.description:
Warum steigt der Bitcoin-Kurs manchmal so stark – und warum fällt er anschließend teilweise genauso heftig wieder?

In dieser Folge schauen wir uns die großen Bitcoin-Zyklen genauer an. Wir sprechen darüber, was ein Chart überhaupt zeigt, was mit Bullenmarkt und Bärenmarkt gemeint ist und welche Rolle das Bitcoin-Halving dabei spielt.

Außerdem werfen wir einen Blick auf die großen Kursphasen der vergangenen Jahre und darauf, warum bei Bitcoin so häufig vom sogenannten Vierjahreszyklus gesprochen wird.

Dabei ist mir besonders wichtig: Solche Muster sind keine Garantie für die Zukunft. Der Bitcoin-Markt verändert sich, neue Marktteilnehmer kommen hinzu und auch wirtschaftliche und politische Entwicklungen können den Kurs beeinflussen.

Zum Schluss geht es noch um meinen persönlichen Blick auf den langfristigen Bitcoin-Chart: Warum ich versuche, mich von kurzfristigen Schwankungen nicht verrückt machen zu lassen, weshalb Geduld für mich eine große Rolle spielt und warum ich Bärenmärkte anders betrachte als reine Verlustphasen.

Wie immer gilt: Dieser Podcast dient ausschließlich der Wissensvermittlung rund um Bitcoin und stellt keine Anlage- oder Finanzberatung dar. Bitte überprüft meine Aussagen selbst und bildet euch eure eigene Meinung.

item.itunes:summary:
Warum steigt der Bitcoin-Kurs manchmal so stark – und warum fällt er anschließend teilweise genauso heftig wieder?

In dieser Folge schauen wir uns die großen Bitcoin-Zyklen genauer an. Wir sprechen darüber, was ein Chart überhaupt zeigt, was mit Bullenmarkt und Bärenmarkt gemeint ist und welche Rolle das Bitcoin-Halving dabei spielt.

Außerdem werfen wir einen Blick auf die großen Kursphasen der vergangenen Jahre und darauf, warum bei Bitcoin so häufig vom sogenannten Vierjahreszyklus gesprochen wird.

Dabei ist mir besonders wichtig: Solche Muster sind keine Garantie für die Zukunft. Der Bitcoin-Markt verändert sich, neue Marktteilnehmer kommen hinzu und auch wirtschaftliche und politische Entwicklungen können den Kurs beeinflussen.

Zum Schluss geht es noch um meinen persönlichen Blick auf den langfristigen Bitcoin-Chart: Warum ich versuche, mich von kurzfristigen Schwankungen nicht verrückt machen zu lassen, weshalb Geduld für mich eine große Rolle spielt und warum ich Bärenmärkte anders betrachte als reine Verlustphasen.

Wie immer gilt: Dieser Podcast dient ausschließlich der Wissensvermittlung rund um Bitcoin und stellt keine Anlage- oder Finanzberatung dar. Bitte überprüft meine Aussagen selbst und bildet euch eure eigene Meinung.

item.title: Bright Orange Future – Leigh Cuen: Poet Journalist #010
item.description:
They’re back! The Brothers Klippsten reunite after a two month hiatus. They're joined by seasoned writer and journalist, Leigh Cuen. The gang discusses journalism and how technology has changed legacy media models, creativity in the open-source space, objective reporting, culture shock, and Bitcoin’s impact on a global scale.

Leigh has been busy! She's covered culture, data journalism, social analysis, Bitcoin, human rights, technology, and multimedia production, and is co-founder of ONA Jerusalem, the first Online News Association group in the Middle East.

Her work has been featured in publications such as Newsweek Japan, International Business Times, Racked, CoinDesk, Insider, History Today, Mic, Al Jazeera, YNet, The Jerusalem Post, Mic, and Salon. Leigh’s work has also been published in Spanish, French, Italian, Hebrew and Arabic.

item.title: Show Me The Bitcoin! Por Standard 21 – Comprar una casa parece imposible: ¿puede Bitcoin cambiarlo? - Aldona Żukowska-Caramés - SMTB EP. 25
item.description:
₿ ¿Podrías ahorrar para comprar una casa en 7 años gracias a Bitcoin? ¿Y si pudieras pagar tus compras, acceder a financiación y utilizar tus ahorros en Bitcoin sin tener que venderlos?


En este episodio de Show Me The Bitcoin hablamos con Aldona Zukowska-Caramés sobre el futuro del dinero, la adopción de las criptomonedas y las nuevas oportunidades que están apareciendo en el sistema financiero. Analizamos la estrategia de Michael Saylor, las tesorerías corporativas, los préstamos respaldados por activos digitales y cómo plataformas como Invity están acercando las finanzas a nuevos usuarios.


En este episodio aprenderás:


🏠 Cómo Bitcoin puede transformar tu capacidad de ahorro y qué posibilidades ofrece para alcanzar objetivos tan importantes como comprar una vivienda.


💳 Cómo utilizar Bitcoin en tu vida cotidiana, pagar con una tarjeta Visa vinculada a tus activos y acceder a liquidez mediante préstamos con Bitcoin como garantía.


🏢 Por qué cada vez más empresas incorporan Bitcoin a sus tesorerías y cuáles son las señales fundamentales para distinguir una estrategia financiera sólida de una operación especulativa.


🚀 Qué oportunidades están surgiendo con la adopción de Bitcoin, cómo evoluciona su relación con la banca tradicional y qué papel pueden desempeñar las nuevas soluciones financieras.


Además, profundizamos en las decisiones de Michael Saylor y Strategy, el debate sobre cuándo conviene vender Bitcoin, los riesgos de determinadas estrategias de inversión y la importancia de adaptar las decisiones financieras a las necesidades de cada persona.


Si te interesa entender hacia dónde evolucionan Bitcoin, el ahorro y las finanzas, esta conversación te ayudará a descubrir nuevas posibilidades, cuestionar algunas creencias habituales y comprender cómo los activos digitales pueden integrarse en la economía cotidiana. Una oportunidad para ampliar tu perspectiva sobre el dinero y tomar decisiones mejor informadas.

item.title: The Path to Bitcoin – Episode #196 – What Wealth Is
item.description:
Most people misjudge Bitcoin because they have never been given a working definition of wealth. David Deutsch's is the set of transformations you could perform without generating new knowledge, and it explains why a million dollars on a deserted island buys almost nothing, why no fortune in 1924 could buy a cure that didn't exist yet, and why holding a fixed share of a ledger gets more valuable as other people solve problems.

Episode Summary

David Deutsch defines the wealth of an entity, in his 2012 paper Constructor Theory, as the set of transformations it could perform without generating new knowledge. That sentence is the best definition of wealth this show has come across, and the episode argues that its absence is what holds most people back from understanding what Bitcoin will do to the extended order, Hayek's name for the collective of people who generate and share knowledge they could never hold individually. Without a definition, money looks like a score to be accumulated. With one, money becomes a tool, and a tool can be judged by what it lets its holder do.

Consider a person stranded on a deserted island with a million dollars. They may know how to bake bread or dig a well, but with no oven, no shovel and no novel arrangements of matter to hand, they can transform almost nothing, and so they are not wealthy. Hand someone a shovel without the knowledge of what digging is for and the result is the same, since an arrangement of matter nobody knows how to employ opens no new phase space. Knowledge also changes how tools are judged. Two shovels with the same blade, one with a six-inch handle and one with a six-foot handle, look equally good to someone who has never dug a hole. The digger knows the long handle spends less energy for the same hole, and finishing in three blocks of time instead of six leaves three blocks, and the energy that would have gone into them, free for other transformations. Time works much like Bitcoin's blocks: standing in one spot to dig commits that moment and removes every future that would have followed from standing a step to the left, just as confirming a transaction removes the branches it would have opened had it stayed in the mempool.

The qualifier at the end of Deutsch's sentence carries the argument. Generating new knowledge is creativity, a separate quantity, and wealth is a set of transformations, which is why it resists being reduced to a single number. Calvin Coolidge Jr., the sixteen-year-old son of a sitting American president, died of blood poisoning from an infected blister on 7 July 1924. His family had about as much money and access as anyone alive, and there was nothing to buy, because Alexander Fleming's report of penicillin's antibacterial action was still years away. Once someone had built the road to that phase space, money could pay for the trip; before then, no amount of it could. Wealth describes the possibilities that already exist, and new knowledge is what enlarges them.

Explanatory knowledge is what gives people an advantage over replicative knowledge, the slower kind evolution produces. Evolution has to build fifty birds with fifty slightly different wings and let the losers die. A mind can conjecture why one design should outperform the rest, criticise the guess, and build only the survivor, running the whole competition in imagination at almost no energy cost. The episode returns to the image of the potter's jug: creativity takes the available information, arranges it into a new order and constrains it so it can't drift anywhere else, which makes a new region of possibilities reachable. Knowledge that does this persists only if it can travel from one physical medium to another while staying hard to vary, and most of what anyone uses each day was inherited this way from people they will never meet.

That inheritance also explains how holders of Bitcoin get wealthier. In the extended order a person earns money by solving other people's problems: if a task would cost someone three blocks of time and a certain amount of energy and you can do it in one, they will willingly hand over a slice of what you saved them. The highest-paid solutions are the ones that keep working without their author, carried in a book, a podcast or a stranger's conference talk. Somewhere, every day, people are producing those solutions, and the set of transformations the extended order can reliably perform keeps growing. The show's older name for that growing pie is TASOE, the total accessible supply of energy. Bitcoin's supply doesn't grow with it. The percentage of the ledger a holder owns stays fixed while the capabilities that percentage commands expand. Deutsch has said nothing about Bitcoin, and this application of his definition is the show's own extension.

The episode also records an error. The early thesis held that Bitcoin had perfected money and coordination, and that people would recognise it. Bitcoin turned out to be the perfect tool for the people who already wanted one. Most people are underwater, unable to think ten days out, let alone ten years. Professionals who manage other people's money face a different trap: beating a colleague by two points on a product nobody questions earns a bonus, while holding a volatile new asset through one bad year gets them fired, and the extra thirty percent they forgo belongs to someone else anyway. Michael Saylor's refinery analogy points to the practical answer: give people the product they want and do the conversion for them. Debasement will keep pushing a few individuals toward the exits, and adoption will come from them long before it comes from the masses.

Maximising wealth therefore means maximising knowledge generation, and the recipe is old: property rights to encourage conjecture and free speech to permit criticism. Both are rare in practice because institutions lock in and stop accepting criticism, and every point of friction between knowledge generation and the extended order leaves everyone worse off. Knowledge also has to outlive the people who discover it. A life works much like a model's context window: understanding builds up through conjecture and criticism, and whatever isn't constrained into a durable, hard-to-vary form disappears when the window closes, so that someone else has to rediscover it at full cost. Every conversation with a large language model starts over unless it is pointed at a second brain that holds context between sessions, the situation of the film 50 First Dates. Rediscovery is waste, and a civilisation that keeps forgetting is less likely to persist against one that remembers.

Seen at the largest scale, most of the order in the universe so far came from structural knowledge, the formation of stars and the interactions of matter under physical law, and then from replicative knowledge, in which every branch has to survive before anything can be learned from it. Explanatory knowledge makes the same leaps with far less energy and fewer blocks of time, and its rate of order generation will keep accelerating. The people who open closed phase space for others will be paid willingly for the new transformations they make possible, and the money they will want is the one hardest to vary. That leaves the episode optimistic and pessimistic at once: confident that Bitcoin will keep operating as it has since inception, and doubtful that most people will recognise what it is in time. The short run will stay volatile, the long run is clear, and the opportunity is still open to anyone willing to do the work.

01:10 - Explanatory knowledge and the fifty wings evolution has to build

02:36 - The jug, the clay and reach

02:59 - A million dollars on a deserted island

03:47 - A shovel you don't know how to use

04:07 - Persistence: maintaining a unique arrangement

05:06 - Back to explaining Bitcoin: money as a tool

05:40 - Short handle, long handle

06:28 - Energy and blocks of time saved

07:04 - Time as blocks, and the futures a commitment removes

08:29 - Inherited knowledge and states that travel

09:04 - Easy to replicate, hard to vary

09:57 - Is more money the answer?

10:10 - Without generating new knowledge: wealth as a set

10:37 - Calvin Coolidge Jr. and the cure money couldn't buy

11:29 - Why holding Bitcoin generates wealth

12:01 - Getting paid for solving other people's problems

12:25 - Knowledge that keeps solving problems without you

13:50 - The perfect tool, for the few who want one

14:18 - People who can't think ten days out

14:46 - Career risk and other people's money

16:10 - Debasement and the forced-adoption thesis

16:58 - Moving fifty thousand dollars: fiat friction versus Bitcoin

17:43 - A few individuals looking for the exits

18:55 - TASOE: a fixed ledger over a growing set

20:01 - Property rights, free speech and lock-in

21:07 - AI and the context window

23:21 - 50 First Dates and the second brain

Timestamps are approximate.

Topics Discussed

  • Wealth: what individuals and the extended order should be optimising for, and why most people misjudge Bitcoin without a definition of it
  • David Deutsch's definition of wealth as the set of transformations one could perform without generating new knowledge
  • The deserted island: why money without tools or knowledge transforms nothing
  • Tools judged by purpose: the short-handled and long-handled shovel
  • Time measured in blocks, and the futures a commitment removes
  • Wealth as a set of possibilities, and creativity as the act that enlarges it
  • Calvin Coolidge Jr. and the transformation no fortune could buy in 1924
  • Explanatory knowledge versus replicative knowledge: conjecture and criticism instead of fifty wings
  • Knowledge as states that travel, easy to replicate and hard to vary
  • Earning money by solving other people's problems, and solutions that work without their author
  • TASOE, the total accessible supply of energy, as the growing pie a fixed-supply ledger lays claim to
  • The early Bitcoin thesis and why most people don't want the perfect tool
  • Career risk for people managing other people's money
  • Property rights, free speech and institutional lock-in
  • The context window: knowledge that disappears unless it is constrained into durable form

Links & References

  • David Deutsch, "Constructor Theory" (arXiv:1210.7439, 2012; Synthese 190, 2013), section 3.9 on wealth
  • David Deutsch, The Beginning of Infinity (Allen Lane, 2011) on explanatory knowledge, creativity, and conjecture and criticism
  • Alexander Fleming, "On the Antibacterial Action of Cultures of a Penicillium" (British Journal of Experimental Pathology, 1929)
  • Calvin Coolidge Presidential Foundation, "Calvin Jr. Dies"
  • F. A. Hayek, The Fatal Conceit: The Errors of Socialism (University of Chicago Press, 1988) on the extended order
  • Karl Popper, Conjectures and Refutations: The Growth of Scientific Knowledge (Routledge, 1963)

Related Episodes

  • Episode #194 - States that Travel covers knowledge as arrangements that travel between substrates, and value as opening phase space for others.
  • Episode #183 - Capital in the 22nd Century treats wealth as embodied knowledge against wealth as a stock of things.
  • Episode #140 - The One Problem is the show's first use of Deutsch's framing of wealth as a repertoire of transformations.

Notable Pull Quotes

““Wealth isn’t a number, it’s a set.”*”

““No amount of money could have bought it the week before.”*”

““Money is just a tool inside of that system to get access to other people’s knowledge.”*”

““Knowledge, especially explanatory knowledge, is states that travel.”*”

““It was the perfect tool for me. It’s not the perfect tool for the masses.”*”

]]>

Ondernemers willen een betrouwbare overheid, maar krijgen die niet, waarschuwt de topman van DSM. Het uitknijpen van DGA’s in box 2, de extreem hoge tarieven in box 3 en het kapotmaken van complete sectoren - waaronder de Nederlandse crypto- en edelmetaalsector, waarin meer dan twee miljoen beleggers actief zijn - worden door de Nederlandse politiek afgedaan als kleine bijkomstigheden.Ondertussen wordt van beleggers verwacht dat zij zelf hun reële rendement bijhouden. Dan is de vraag: wie gaat die gegevens aanleveren? Sommige banken en brokers kunnen deze informatie niet leveren. Ook is er nog geen toets geweest bij de Belastingdienst. Beleggers geven ondertussen aan dat zij hun reële rendement zullen berekenen na aftrek van onder meer inflatie, transactiekosten bij brokers, valutakosten en abonnementskosten.Kortom: het was een drama, het is een drama en het zal waarschijnlijk een drama blijven. Sterker nog: zelfs de man die aan de wieg stond van de wet spreekt zich inmiddels uit. Zijn boodschap: weg met de novelle, trek de wet in en kom met een nieuw wetsontwerp.Daarnaast neemt de onrust in Frankrijk toe, nu de rente daar blijft oplopen. Zelfs in Nederland beginnen we daar de gevolgen van te voelen. En ligt er oorlog op de loer? Nederland voert de druk op Rusland verder op…Kortom: genoeg te bespreken. Welkom bij deze nieuwe aflevering van Madelon Praat.

item.title: The Cryptocurrency Podcast: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Blockchain, Stablecoins, DeFi, Altcoins, Crypto Markets, Regulation, Mining, and the Future of Digital Money – Crypto Investing Lessons From Ethereum’s History
item.description:
This episode traces Ethereum’s evolution as a case study for investors—examining the DAO hack, DeFi boom, NFT rise, gas costs, the Merge and EIP‑1559, Layer‑2 scaling, competing chains, governance dynamics, regulatory pressures, and security lessons that shaped how people invest in the platform.

item.description:
How do you keep your cryptocurrency safe? You have to follow some crypto security best practices.

In this episode, we chat with Ruben Merre, CEO of NGRAVE, about how users can protect their funds. Ruben explains what can be done, why other hard wallets can be vulnerable and how NGRAVE Zero fixes that.

item.title: Nerd Culture • A Gamekings Podcast – #280 over VisionQuest, Godzilla Minus One & Widow's Bay
item.description:
Het is tijd voor Nerd Culture #280! Deze week zitten Koos, Huey en Jelle weer met z'n drieën aan tafel voor een bomvolle aflevering over films, series en het laatste nieuws uit Hollywood. We bespreken onder andere de eerste beelden van Blade Runner 2099, de opvallende ontwikkelingen rondom The Batman Part II en het laatste nieuws uit het DC-universum, waaronder Clayface, Man of Tomorrow en de mogelijke toekomst van Batman Beyond.

Ook bespreken we de betrokkenheid van Paul Verhoeven bij de nieuwe RoboCop-serie. Daarnaast hebben we natuurlijk weer flink wat films en series gekeken, waaronder Godzilla Minus One, Ted Lasso, Slow Horses, Reacher en Star Trek. Genoeg te bespreken dus in deze nieuwe aflevering van Nerd Culture!

Marvel's VisionQuest Review

Marvel breidt het MCU verder uit met VisionQuest, de serie waarin Paul Bettany terugkeert als Vision na de gebeurtenissen uit WandaVision. In deze nieuwe productie staat de zoektocht van Vision naar zijn identiteit centraal. Wat betekent het om menselijk te zijn als je eigenlijk een kunstmatig wezen bent? En hoe gaat Vision om met zijn verleden en de herinneringen aan Wanda Maximoff? In Nerd Culture #280 bespreken Koos, Huey en Jelle de serie uitgebreid. Hoe sterk is het verhaal, wat vinden we van de personages en weet Marvel met VisionQuest opnieuw het niveau van WandaVision te bereiken? Ook kijken we naar de betekenis van de serie voor de toekomst van het Marvel Cinematic Universe.

Steven Soderbergh neemt opnames The Batman Part II over van Matt Reeves

Opvallend nieuws rondom The Batman Part II! Regisseur Matt Reeves heeft de opnames van het langverwachte vervolg met Robert Pattinson tijdelijk moeten stilleggen vanwege familieomstandigheden. Gelukkig krijgt hij hulp uit onverwachte hoek: niemand minder dan Oscarwinnaar Steven Soderbergh, bekend van Ocean's Eleven en Traffic, neemt de laatste weken van de opnames voor zijn rekening. Soderbergh heeft zichzelf aangeboden om Reeves te helpen en benadrukt dat hij diens visie volledig wil respecteren. Reeves blijft dan ook verantwoordelijk voor de film en zal de montage en nabewerking weer oppakken zodra hij terugkeert. Ondertussen staat de bioscooprelease nog altijd gepland voor 18 februari 2028. Maar wat betekent de betrokkenheid van een regisseur als Soderbergh voor het eindresultaat? En moeten we ons na alle eerdere vertragingen opnieuw zorgen maken over The Batman Part II?

Wil je adverteren bij de podcast Nerd Culture óf misschien bij een andere podcast van ILVY Network? Mail dan naar management@ilvy.com en/of kijk even op de website: https://ilvy.com/podcast

See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.

]]>
